stories.title: MIT-WPU students design algae-based building facade
stories.summary: Students at MIT-WPU have developed porous coatings using algae, moss and cyanobacteria to cool building surfaces by up to 3°C. The team claims the biological growth provides a natural alternative to air conditioning. The project was created for the Youth for Earth Campaign 2026.

stories.title: MIT-WPU students develop living facade for passive cooling
stories.summary: A team from MIT World Peace University has introduced a bioreceptive facade system using living biological surfaces to address rising temperatures in Indian cities. The project aims to explore passive cooling methods for buildings by integrating algae and cyanobacteria directly onto exterior walls.

stories.title: Passivhaus standard may reduce repair costs, says Barratt London
stories.summary: Building homes to the Passivhaus standard will reduce long-term repair spending, according to the head of design at Barratt London. Attzaz Rashid made the comments during a panel discussion at the Passivhaus Trust conference held this Wednesday.

stories.title: Peabody and Higgins finish Deptford Passivhaus project
stories.summary: Peabody and Higgins have completed a development in Deptford featuring 189 homes built to Passivhaus standards. The project uses triple-glazed windows and sealed walls to maintain internal temperatures. It is part of a larger regeneration scheme expected to deliver 1,500 homes in total.

stories.title: Magicbricks launches sustainable real estate index
stories.summary: Magicbricks and the School of Planning and Architecture in Delhi have launched an index assessing ten Indian cities on sustainable development readiness. The report evaluates infrastructure, environmental risk and investment potential across major urban markets to determine how cities scale sustainable real estate.

stories.title: Fabric formwork reduces concrete use in beams
stories.summary: MIT researchers found that software-designed concrete beams cast in fabric formwork require one-third of the concrete and half the steel of conventional beams. The design uses angled legs to remove material while maintaining load-bearing capacity. The process translates software models into flat fabric patterns.

stories.title: Magicbricks and SPA Delhi rank cities on sustainability
stories.summary: Magicbricks and the School of Planning and Architecture in Delhi have launched an index ranking ten Indian cities on their readiness for sustainable real estate. The report aims to identify where sustainable development offers the strongest risk-adjusted returns for investors.

stories.title: Climate change increases repair risks for historic buildings
stories.summary: Extreme weather is increasing maintenance requirements for UK heritage properties. The Environment Agency estimates 6.3 million properties in England are currently in flood-prone areas, a figure that could rise to eight million by 2050. Repairs must adhere to strict conservation standards, increasing costs.

stories.title: Bhoomi puja scheduled for Malakpet housing project
stories.summary: The Telangana Housing Board plans to perform a bhoomi puja for the Indiramma Illu Towers in Malakpet soon. Officials have been directed to complete the 480-flat project within one year. The scheme is intended to provide housing for low-income families in urban areas.

stories.title: Bhopal municipal body targets illegal construction
stories.summary: The Bhopal Municipal Corporation has intensified enforcement against unauthorized construction and commercial activities in residential areas. Commissioner Ramprakash Ahirwar directed the building permission wing to take immediate action against violations. A hearing on the city master plan is currently ongoing.

stories.title: Embassy Developments launches luxury residences in Bengaluru
stories.summary: Embassy Developments has launched 59 ultra-luxury homes at Embassy ONE in Bengaluru. The project has a gross development value of 1,400 crore rupees and includes managed services for residents. The site is located at the intersection of several established residential neighborhoods.

stories.title: Pecan Realty and HDFC Capital partner for Mumbai project
stories.summary: Pecan Realty and HDFC Capital have formed a partnership to develop institutional-quality commercial real estate in Mumbai. Their first project is a 1,000 crore rupee mixed-use development in Andheri East. The collaboration aims to build a long-term pipeline of high-quality assets.

stories.title: Supreme Court protects homebuyers in stalled project
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has restrained coercive action against 4,500 homebuyers in a stalled Bengaluru project. The court directed that no action be taken until possession is granted, noting that buyers have already paid 95 percent of the sale consideration to the insolvent firm.

stories.title: Notandas Realty begins Notan House handover - Construction Week India
Centre seeks Supreme Court hearing on builder agreements
stories.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has requested an early hearing on a petition pending since 2020 regarding uniform builder-buyer agreements. The government aims to protect consumers from one-sided contract terms in the real estate sector.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court freezes construction on Jaypee Greens land
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered an immediate freeze on new construction and third-party rights across 236 acres of land allotted for the Jaypee Greens Golf Course. The interim order follows a petition filed by the golf course members association.

stories.title: India-US trade deal awaits tariff clarity
stories.summary: The signing of an India-US trade deal depends on Washington finalizing its tariff architecture and concluding ongoing Section 301 investigations, according to Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal. Negotiations for the first tranche of the agreement are nearing completion.

stories.title: Sany IROOTECH headquarters named best tall building
stories.summary: The Council on Vertical Urbanism named the Sany IROOTECH Headquarters in Guangzhou the 2026 Best Tall Building Worldwide. The development features two towers wrapped in an exposed diamond grid of concrete-filled steel tubes. Four of every five floors are suspended from the structural frame.

stories.title: JSWD to design RIYMAR towers in Riyadh
stories.summary: JSWD has won an international competition to design the RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The mixed-use project will include residential, hospitality, office, and retail spaces. The development aims to contribute to the city's evolving urban identity under the Vision 2030 initiative.

stories.title: Sid Lee Architecture completes Ontario hotel
stories.summary: Sid Lee Architecture has unveiled The Clayfield Hotel in Niagara-on-the-Lake. The 94,000-square-foot curved-glass building includes 60 rooms, a restaurant, and a ballroom. Architect Martin Leblanc described the project as a hub where wine culture and hospitality find a home.

stories.title: SHoP Architects unveils Miami supertall design
stories.summary: SHoP Architects has released designs for a 1,049-foot-tall skyscraper in Miami. The project is backed by tennis player Novak Djokovic and will house amenities for the luxury brand ATMA. If completed, the tower would exceed the height of the city's current tallest skyscraper.

stories.title: Perkins&Will and Estúdio Campana design airport lounge
stories.summary: Perkins&Will and Estúdio Campana have designed the 1,400-square-meter Pedra Preta Lounge in São Paulo’s Guarulhos International Airport. The interior features a curved timber entrance installation modeled on the Amazon’s Juruá River. The lounge is located within the airport's Terminal 3.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival announces first winners
stories.summary: The World Architecture Festival has completed its first day of events in Fort Lauderdale. The three-day festival features over 400 live pitches from finalists competing for 23 award categories. Winners announced on the first day include Studio Lotus, Foster + Partners, and Haptic Architects.

stories.title: Daichi sauna named architecture project of the year
stories.summary: The Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna in Kanagawa, Japan, has been named Architecture Project of the Year at the 2026 Dezeen Awards. The treetop sauna was designed around existing trees as integral structural elements. The project also won the Leisure and Wellness category.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival Day One winners
stories.summary: The 2026 World Architecture Festival has announced its first award winners at the Broward County Convention Center. The event hosts over 400 live pitches from finalists across 23 categories. Winners include Studio Lotus, Foster + Partners, Warren and Mahoney, and Haptic Architects.

stories.title: BIG proposes timber district in Switzerland
stories.summary: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for four timber buildings in Thun, Switzerland. The 13,000-square-meter development includes two hotels and residential buildings with stacked wooden volumes that project above the street. The design is set against the Bernese Alps.

stories.title: Mass timber offers alternative to steel and concrete
stories.summary: Mass timber is gaining ground as a building method for tall structures. Layers of lumber are stacked with alternating grain directions and bonded into panels. While traditional lumber lacks the strength for skyscrapers, these engineered panels are designed to support larger structures.

stories.title: Researchers optimize sustainable concrete
stories.summary: A research team has engineered high-strength structural concrete using modified limestone calcined clay cement. The study coupled multi-criteria decision analysis with Taguchi experimental design to overcome engineering obstacles. The method aims to improve the use of low-clinker binders in construction.

stories.title: Shawmut completes Brooklyn library timber installation
stories.summary: Shawmut Design and Construction has finished the mass timber installation for the new Canarsie Library in Brooklyn. The structure uses 38 cross-laminated timber panels and over 200 glulam beams and columns. Project executive Joe Boyle noted that mass timber allows for faster construction with less disruption.

stories.title: Peabody and Higgins complete Passivhaus scheme
stories.summary: Peabody and Higgins have completed a Passivhaus development at Deptford Landings, delivering 189 social and affordable homes. The project uses highly insulated envelopes and airtight construction to reduce space-heating demand. The scheme highlights a growing demand for large-scale, low-energy residential blocks.

stories.title: Autodesk and Neilsoft open Pune centre
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft have partnered to establish a Centre of Excellence in Pune. The facility will combine Autodesk’s cloud-based AECO platform with Neilsoft’s digital twin capabilities. The initiative aims to accelerate the adoption of BIM and digital twin technology across global markets.

stories.title: Construction industry prepares for 2027 BIM leap
Review explores wood species for mass timber
stories.summary: A systematic review of 189 peer-reviewed articles has evaluated the structural characteristics of mass timber products. The research explores expanding the current range of wood species used in manufacturing. Mass timber is increasingly used for high-rise buildings due to its mechanical performance and carbon sequestration.

stories.title: ICON begins printing largest commercial building
stories.summary: ICON has started 3D printing a 1,175-square-meter training center for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio. The building pairs 3D printed walls with a steel superstructure. The project is the first to use ICON’s full design-build model, with completion expected in summer 2027.

stories.title: Official inspects Smart City projects in Haryana
stories.summary: Deputy Commissioner Anand Kumar Sharma inspected ongoing Smart City projects at Karna Stadium, including hostels and a multipurpose hall. He directed officials to expedite the work to ensure the facilities are completed and inaugurated shortly. The projects are valued at approximately 24 crore rupees.

stories.title: Chief Secretary reviews Smart City projects in Jammu
stories.summary: Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav, the new Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir, conducted an early-morning field visit to Jammu city on Thursday. The trip was intended to assess urban infrastructure and sanitation arrangements. The city is currently undergoing various developmental initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life.

stories.title: Bhubaneswar and Cuttack brace for Cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: Bhubaneswar and Cuttack are preparing for heavy rainfall and potential flooding as Cyclone Akvan approaches the Odisha coast. The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange warning for the region, forecasting winds up to 80 kmph. Landfall is expected by Friday afternoon.

stories.title: Rainfall continues in Odisha ahead of Akvan
stories.summary: Incessant rain hit Bhubaneswar and Cuttack on Thursday as Cyclone Akvan neared the coast. While authorities reported minor damage to trees and localized waterlogging, officials stated the rainfall has not yet been heavy enough to trigger major flooding. The storm is expected to make landfall by Friday.

stories.title: J&K Chief Secretary reviews Jammu’s urban development, sanitation projects - The Hawk
MCD estimates 40 lakh man-hours for building safety survey
stories.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has informed the government that a preliminary safety survey of 40 lakh buildings will require 40 lakh man-hours. The civic body is currently developing uniform assessment criteria for the project, which will involve multiple departments to collate data into a comprehensive database.

stories.title: Bengaluru pilots ward-level climate action plans
stories.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has launched climate planning initiatives across five pilot wards to address urban flooding and water shortages. The project aims to integrate better drainage, rainwater management and urban greening into neighbourhood-level infrastructure. The city is currently navigating the challenges of balancing rapid expansion with environmental resilience.

stories.title: HYDRAA explores groundwater recharge to mitigate flooding
stories.summary: The HYDRAA Commissioner held discussions with scientists on Wednesday regarding groundwater recharge and flood prevention in Hyderabad. The meeting focused on identifying sites for new lakes and stepwells to capture rainwater. Officials are currently assessing how much rainfall the city can feasibly retain to reduce flood risks.

stories.title: Bhubaneswar activates emergency cyclone measures
stories.summary: The Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation has identified 93 cyclone shelters and placed its disaster response teams on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan. Personnel have been directed to remain on duty for emergency evacuations and tree removal. The city is preparing for what is expected to be medium-intensity impact.

stories.title: STARS summit leverages AI for Dubai tree planting
stories.summary: Experts at the STARS summit are using AI to support a project to plant 1.5 million trees in Dubai. The initiative is part of broader discussions at Dubai Future Week regarding the role of technology in urban development and environmental management.

stories.title: STARS Summit examines the future of resilient cities
stories.summary: The STARS Summit at Dubai Future Week is exploring how urban science and technology can make cities more adaptable to human needs. MIT's Senseable City Lab is hosting sessions on sensing and mobility. The event brings together researchers to discuss how emerging technologies might reshape the modern urban landscape.

stories.title: NYC proposes fees for new waste containers
stories.summary: The New York City Department of Sanitation is proposing a fee of up to $55 per bin to cover the installation and maintenance of its expanded waste containerization program. The city is currently rolling out these bins to additional neighborhoods to manage refuse collection.

stories.title: Climate change recovery remains a financial challenge
stories.summary: Farmers in Pakistan’s Sindh province continue to struggle with land recovery four years after severe flooding destroyed crops and homes. The incident highlights the ongoing difficulty of financing the human and economic costs of climate change. Many regions remain unable to return to previous levels of cultivation.

stories.title: Kathmandu to Host Climate Action Week from December 7-13 - Hamro Patro
Tamil Nadu revives Olympic city plans for Chennai
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has restarted planning for an Olympic city on 124 acres in Semmancheri, Chennai. The Public Works Department has invited firms to submit designs for the facility and five additional sports centres across the state. The project was previously announced as a major infrastructure priority.

stories.title: Mountain climate impacts discussed at COP31
stories.summary: Despite the rejection of a formal agenda item on high mountain ranges, COP31 talks in Türkiye have focused on the catastrophic impacts of rising temperatures on these regions. The World Meteorological Organization has highlighted the urgent need to address environmental fragility in high-altitude areas.

stories.title: COP31 leaders focus on resilient urban infrastructure
stories.summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum emphasized the need for climate action to be implemented within the homes and infrastructure of cities. The Presidency announced two new initiatives, including a compact for energy-efficient buildings, citing post-earthquake reconstruction as a model for resilient development.

stories.title: India remains high on climate risk index
stories.summary: A report citing the Climate Risk Index 2027 indicates that India remains among the countries most vulnerable to extreme weather events. The analysis links fatalities and economic losses to recurring hazards like floods and cyclones. The findings have renewed questions regarding the resilience of current urban infrastructure designs.

stories.title: Chenghengwei secures funding for edge AI chip production
stories.summary: Chenghengwei has raised nearly RMB 200 million in Series A funding to scale production of its CH37 edge AI chip. The company claims the chip integrates CPU, GPU and NPU functions to reduce system complexity. Backers are expected to provide ecosystem resources alongside the capital injection.

stories.title: Rockwell sets boundaries for AI agents in digital twin simulations
stories.summary: Rockwell Automation now requires that AI agents only execute digital twin simulations supported by a validated model. The company has established green, yellow and red zones to dictate where virtual tests may replace physical ones. Engineering questions are currently limited to one or two per session.

stories.title: Iconic secures $10 million to apply AI to infrastructure projects
stories.summary: Amsterdam-based Iconic has raised $10 million in seed funding to develop AI software for large capital projects like energy grids and transport infrastructure. The startup aims to address inefficiencies in a sector where $15 trillion is invested annually. Peak Capital led the investment round.

stories.title: GlassPoint raises $24 million for industrial heat decarbonization
stories.summary: Solar-powered industrial heat specialist GlassPoint has secured $24 million in funding led by N.I.S. New Investment Solutions. The round brings the company's total 2026 funding to $44 million. The investment targets the decarbonization of energy-intensive industrial processes, a sector increasingly distinct from traditional solar power generation.

stories.title: Pegasus Tech Ventures and Taisei launch $150 million construction fund
stories.summary: Pegasus Tech Ventures and Taisei Corporation are establishing a $150 million corporate venture capital fund to invest in construction technology. The fund will support AI, robotics and digital twin startups over a 10-year period. Pegasus will serve as the general partner for the new initiative.

stories.title: Supersede raises $13M to enter construction market - Plastics News
Rayon releases V4 with 3D modeling and agentic AI
stories.summary: Rayon has launched V4 of its browser-based design software, adding 3D modeling and agentic AI tools in beta. Co-founder Stanislas Chaillou stated the company aims to occupy the market gap between AutoCAD and SketchUp. The product remains focused on interiors.

stories.title: Renda and Nexalus debut liquid-cooled AI server
stories.summary: The Renda Nova8 is a 4U AI server featuring eight liquid-cooled Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. The design allows the cards to fit into a standard 19-inch air-cooled rack without additional infrastructure. Each GPU operates at its full 600W capacity within a single-slot configuration.

stories.title: Birmingham City University receives funding for AI energy twin
stories.summary: Birmingham City University has been awarded £50,000 to develop an AI-powered digital twin for community energy management. The project aims to help businesses and residents anticipate demand and reduce carbon emissions. It combines energy data with virtual testing to inform infrastructure decisions.

stories.title: Clarion-Limestone students showcase manufacturing skills
stories.summary: Clarion-Limestone High School hosted an open house to demonstrate its Lion Manufacturing program. Students produced parts using 3D printing, welding and woodworking for local consumers. The program, supported by grants and donations, aims to prepare the next generation of business owners for the manufacturing industry.

stories.title: India faces pressure to integrate chemical safety regulations
stories.summary: The Global Framework on Chemicals conference in Geneva has highlighted India's lack of a comprehensive chemical safety system. Experts argue that as the country seeks to expand its manufacturing economy, it must address fragmented regulation and monitoring. The event concludes on November 20.

stories.title: Chris Williamson criticizes architectural regulatory system
stories.summary: Chris Williamson has resigned from the Architects Registration Board register, citing a desire to challenge the current regulatory process. He argues that the system has become absurd. Williamson previously served as an architect for several decades after being inspired by professional codes of conduct.

stories.title: Harvard students propose alternatives to Triumphal Arch
stories.summary: Two Harvard landscape architecture students have developed conceptual designs for Washington, D.C.'s Memorial Circle. The proposals follow a federal judge's decision to block the construction of a 250-foot-tall Triumphal Arch. The judge recently extended the order preventing the project from moving forward.

stories.title: Montana State students earn national healthcare design recognition
stories.summary: Montana State University students have received national recognition for their work in healthcare design. The university confirmed the awards following a review of student projects. No further details regarding the specific nature of the designs or the awarding bodies were provided.

stories.title: Sharjah Architecture Triennial features Indian design collectives
stories.summary: The third Sharjah Architecture Triennial, titled Architecture Otherwise, is currently showcasing work from 35 global practitioners. The event includes several Indian artists and collectives focused on civic infrastructure. The exhibition is curated by Vyjayanthi Rao and is scheduled to run until April 14, 2027.

stories.title: Ammodo Architecture Days highlights social practice
stories.summary: The Ammodo Architecture Days event is exploring how architecture influences community development through housing and adaptive reuse. Projects from Barcelona, Accra and the Peruvian Amazon were featured to demonstrate architecture as a social practice. The program is organized by the Ammodo Foundation.

stories.title: Sharjah Architecture Triennial explores collective infrastructure
stories.summary: The third Sharjah Architecture Triennial opened on November 14, 2026, focusing on the theme of building civic infrastructure for collective futures. Curator Vyjayanthi Rao is examining how spatial knowledge shapes social relationships. The event will remain open to the public until April 14, 2027.

stories.title: EU countries request Russia's exclusion from Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Ten European Union countries have signed a diplomatic note urging the European Commission to exclude Russia from the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennial. The group argues that Russian participation would normalize the war in Ukraine. The commission has been asked to provide sustained efforts to maintain the ban.

research.title: This remarkable new material could solve a major carbon capture problem
research.summary: Scientists have developed a new carbon capture material that turns moisture from an obstacle into an advantage, potentially solving a major problem with removing CO2 from industrial emissions. The material works even in extremely humid conditions and can be reused repeatedly, offering a promising path toward cheaper, more.

research.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
research.summary: Deep beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists have discovered tiny hidden ecosystems inside metal-rich rocks that take millions of years to form. Researchers examined 244 nodules and found more than 4,100 animals living in their cracks and cavities, including unique communities unlike those in the surrounding seafloor mud. These.

research.title: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom
research.summary: Scientists have unexpectedly discovered how to control the magnetic spin inside a single atom's nucleus using radio waves, overturning previous assumptions about atomic behavior. The breakthrough could pave the way for more reliable quantum memory, although researchers are still trying to understand why it works.
